clue.text: Shop has dainty cape returned

parts.note: dainty means fine and delicate

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the cape is read from its end

parts.note: a ness is a headland or cape, as in Loch Ness's neighbours

explanation.surface: A boutique stocks a delicate little cape that a customer brought back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' looks like a shop's refund, but it is the turnaround signal. A ness is a headland, as in many Scottish place names.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicatessen is a store selling cooked meats, cheeses and prepared foods.

clue.text: Popular book among detectives — give it up!

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending it up means reading the result from bottom to top
among means placed in the middle of, so the book sits within the detectives

parts.note: the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A best-seller is found among the police, who are told to hand it over.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the British police's plain-clothes detective branch. In a down entry, 'up' asks for the letters to be read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Demotic means of the ordinary people, as in everyday common speech.

clue.text: Cut made by cricket beginner, in a way

indicators.note: in places the selected letter inside the way

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road

indicators.note: the beginner of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of cricket

explanation.surface: A batsman just starting out plays a cut shot, in his way.
explanation.walkthrough: A cut is a cricket stroke, which makes 'cricket beginner' look like a novice player.
explanation.definitionFit: To lance is to cut open with a sharp blade, as a surgeon does a boil.

clue.text: Friar appears to feel concern about me getting settled

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the feeling of concern wraps round what follows

parts.note: to care is to feel concern
taken as written
lit is a past tense of alight, as a bird settles on a branch

explanation.surface: A monk seems worried that I have finally put down roots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settled' looks like the end of the surface story, but it is the bird sense: alighted.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmelites are members of a Catholic mendicant order, whose men are friars.

clue.text: River vessel upset by youth leader

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the vessel upside down, reading it from bottom to top

parts.note: a vat is a large container

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of youth

explanation.surface: A boat on a river capsized by the head of a youth club.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT turned over gives TAV. The Tavy is a river in Devon, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tavy flows off Dartmoor into the Tamar, so it names a real English waterway.

clue.text: Like a relative of R.L.S., yet is different

indicators.note: made different, the letters take on a new order

parts.note: the initials of Robert Louis Stevenson plus two short words

explanation.surface: Comparing someone to a kinsman of Robert Louis Stevenson, though unlike him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of R.L.S.' looks like part of the definition, but the initials are anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisterly means behaving as a sister would, and a sister is a close family member.

clue.text: Score made by player?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in cricket, a run added to the total without coming off the bat
second meaning: a minor actor in a crowd scene

explanation.surface: Points put on the board by some sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bye or wide is credited to the team, not to a batsman, so it is precisely a score no player made.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a run added to a cricket total and a walk-on film actor.

clue.text: Express dissatisfaction with a break in the service

indicators.note: breaking in means forcing a way inside, so the single letter goes into the service

parts.note: Complin, or Compline, is the last church service of the day
taken as written

explanation.surface: Grumbling about an interruption in a church service or a utility.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes into COMPLIN before its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To complain is to say that you are unhappy or annoyed about something.

clue.text: Offer old coins to queen

parts.note: ten d, ten old pennies, d being the pre-1971 British penny
Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Presenting antique money to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Before decimalisation in 1971, British pence were written d, so ten pence was 10d.
explanation.definitionFit: To tender is to present formally, as in tendering a resignation or a bid.

clue.text: Trees from the island woods

parts.note: the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea
groves are small woods

explanation.surface: A description of timber gathered in some island's forests.
explanation.definitionFit: Mangroves are tropical trees growing in coastal swamps, with tangled stilt roots.

clue.text: Left back gets point of the metaphor

indicators.note: going back runs the word for left in the opposite direction

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A football left back grasps the meaning of a figure of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left back' reads as a football position, but it is the sailor's word for left turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A trope is a figure of speech, and a metaphor is the standard example of one.

clue.text: Old city just fails to achieve optimum rating

indicators.note: falling just short means stopping one letter before the end

parts.note: the optimum is the best of all

explanation.surface: An ancient city narrowly misses top marks in some league table.
explanation.walkthrough: THE BEST loses its final T.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes was a great city of ancient Egypt, and also of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Absconded with document about soldiers' quarters, perhaps

indicators.note: about means around, so the document wraps round the soldiers' quarters

parts.note: a deed is a legal document
a camp is one example of where soldiers are quartered

explanation.surface: A deserter ran off carrying papers about the barracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldiers' quarters, perhaps' looks like the definition, but 'perhaps' marks it as one example feeding the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to leave suddenly or secretly, which is exactly what absconding is.

clue.text: Composer was happy as a sand-boy?

definitions.text: Composer was happy as a sand-boy?

parts.note: surface reading: an old saying for someone carefree and cheerful
setter's reading: Sand's boy, the lover of the novelist George Sand

explanation.surface: Some composer was as cheerful as could be.
explanation.walkthrough: George Sand, the French novelist, had a long affair with the Polish composer, so he was Sand's boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopin was the Polish Romantic composer famous for piano works, and George Sand's partner.

clue.text: Shrub reset by dear Noel

indicators.note: something reset is put in place again in a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A bush replanted by someone's beloved Noel.
explanation.definitionFit: Oleander is an evergreen flowering bush, poisonous, common in warm climates.

clue.text: What a pity Rita confounded him!

definitions.note: the answer is a man's name, so 'him' stands for it

indicators.note: confounded means thrown into confusion, so the name's letters are jumbled

parts.note: an exclamation of regret
the letters of the name rearranged

explanation.surface: A sorry tale of a man left baffled by a woman named Rita.
explanation.definitionFit: Alastair is a Scottish man's given name, so it fits a pronoun for a male person.

clue.text: (No way to get) one kind of boundary

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in cricket, purely defensive batting, which is no way to get runs
second meaning: a dry-built field barrier

explanation.surface: A field barrier that nobody can get past.
explanation.walkthrough: Boundary also means a hit to the edge of a cricket field, a four or six, which a stonewalling batsman never tries for.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier of piled stones marks a field's edge, and stonewalling is stubborn, scoreless defence.

clue.text: A criterion in a way — and a different way

parts.note: ST, street, a way to walk or drive along
taken as written
A as written, then RD, road, another kind of way

explanation.surface: A rule of judgment, one way of measuring, alongside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a level or benchmark by which things are judged, which is what a criterion is.

clue.text: Risks increasing figure at board meeting?

definitions.text: Risks increasing figure at board meeting?

parts.note: surface reading: a company directors' meeting where risky figures might rise
setter's reading: board is food on a table, and the figure is one's waistline

explanation.surface: Directors gamble with rising numbers at their meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Board is an old word for a dining table or the meals served at it, as in board and lodging.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who eats too much at a meal risks gaining weight and widening their waistline.

clue.text: Perhaps a native story — eastern sort

indicators.note: to sort is to put in order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: An Eastern tale told by someone born in the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Native' looks like a person, but in Britain a native is an oyster from home beds, such as those at Whitstable in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: A native is a British name for an oyster raised in local, especially Kentish, waters.

clue.text: Canons get fired?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: songs in which voices enter in turn with the same tune

definitions.note: a description, things that get fired, rather than a direct substitute
definitions.meaning: second meaning: cartridges or shells discharged from a gun

explanation.surface: Cathedral clergy are given the sack.
explanation.walkthrough: Canons sounds like cannons, which suits the firing, but here they are musical pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A round is a song sung in canon, and a round is also a single shot of ammunition.

clue.text: What a bet has that a better hasn't — put your shirt on it?

wordplay.words: What a bet has that a better hasn't
wordplay.note: the word bet holds just one of a certain letter, where better holds two

explanation.surface: A gambling tip: bet everything on it, since a bet has more going for it than a gambler.
explanation.walkthrough: Bet has a single T, better has two. Put your shirt on it means bet everything, but here it is literal: the shirt goes over this garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet is a sleeveless vest or undershirt, worn beneath a shirt.

clue.text: Prison offence connected with key duplication

parts.note: a sin is a moral offence
G is a musical key
a duplication is a second copy of what came just before

explanation.surface: A jailbird's crime involved copying the cell keys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key duplication' looks like copying a key, but it is the whole offence-plus-key pair that is doubled.
explanation.definitionFit: Sing Sing is a famous maximum-security jail in New York State.

clue.text: Typewriter?

parts.note: surface reading: a machine for typing letters
setter's reading: a word meaning type, which is also an old pointed writing tool

explanation.walkthrough: Split it as type plus writer: the answer means a type or manner, and is also a stylus for writing on wax.
explanation.definitionFit: Style means a kind or manner, and a style was the pointed instrument used for writing in antiquity.

clue.text: Female's male?

definitions.note: the whole clue points to a man's name

parts.note: the possessive belonging to a woman
a man is a male person

explanation.surface: Asking who a woman's partner is.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as her man, the phrase is also a man's name, which the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: Herman is a masculine given name, literally spelling out a woman's man.

clue.text: Many eager to see the giant

parts.note: M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, stands for many
agog means eagerly expectant

explanation.surface: Crowds keen to catch sight of a giant at a fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Gog and Magog are the legendary giants whose effigies stand in London's Guildhall.

clue.text: Scrutinize bills up North

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom to the top

parts.note: ACs, accounts, are bills
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Checking invoices carefully somewhere in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan is to examine closely, as in scanning a document point by point.

clue.text: Time to fight?

parts.note: surface reading: the moment a battle or bout begins
setter's reading: time is the thing one must fight against, as in the saying time is the foe

explanation.surface: Announcing that the moment for battle has come.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying that time is the foe makes time something to fight, not a moment for fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: An opponent is whoever you fight, and the proverb casts time as that opponent.

clue.text: Port for Michael, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a seaport on the White Sea in northern Russia
second meaning: a chief angel, of whom Michael is one

explanation.surface: A harbour suited to someone called Michael.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael is named in scripture as a chief angel, and the Russian port Arkhangelsk takes the name in English.

clue.text: Perhaps a link with a very influential member?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a link was a torch carried ahead to guide walkers at night
second meaning: the most prominent figure in a group

explanation.surface: A connection to a powerful person in some club or party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Link' suggests a chain or a connection, but it is an old word for a torch.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch carried in front is literally a guiding flame, and figuratively the phrase means a prominent person.
